body.statement:
Use \(L_N(H)\) and \(\delta_\star\) from \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\).  Fix \(0<\alpha<\delta_\star\).  Let \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) be any deterministic map from arm-outcome tables to sets of complete weak orders such that, for every fixed binary schedule satisfying the design and stratified-interference assumptions,
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in
       \mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
If \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) for every compatible \(H\), then in fact
\[
 \mathfrak C_\alpha(H)=\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 \qquad\text{for every compatible }H.
\]
More sharply, if \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\) and \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\), there is a deterministic schedule realizing \(N\) for which the noncoverage probability is at least
\[
 L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\]
Thus no family indexed by all \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) can both preserve uniform coverage at every level and be a strict contained refinement at some compatible table at every level.  This obstruction does not assert impossibility of a consonant strict refinement for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix \((H,N)\in\mathfrak J\).  Every abstract response type is realized by a deterministic binary cluster schedule: for each \(t\in\mathcal T\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\), partition the labeled unit set \(\mathcal I\) into four sets \(I_{t,r}^{ab}\) of respective cardinalities \(N_r^{ab}\), and set
\[
 (Y_i(0,r),Y_i(1,r))=(a,b)
 \qquad\text{for }i\in I_{t,r}^{ab}.
\]
The partitions may be chosen separately across \(r\), because stratified interference imposes no cross-policy restriction on these fixed potential outcomes.  Put copies of this schedule on exactly \(N_t\) labeled clusters.  The resulting schedule is binary, satisfies the stated interference condition, and has true response-count vector \(N^\star=N\).  Under the exact two-stage design, \(\texttt{lem:global-compatible-atom-bound}\) gives
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\}=L_N(H).
\]

Suppose \(\mathcal O(N)\notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\).  On the event \(H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\), the realized schedule has true order \(\mathcal O(N^\star)=\mathcal O(N)\), so that event is contained in the noncoverage event.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{\mathcal O(N^\star)
        \notin\mathfrak C_\alpha(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\}
 &\ge \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\{H^{\mathrm{obs}}=H\}\\
 &=L_N(H)\ge\delta_\star>\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\]
This contradicts the assumed uniform coverage.  Therefore a uniformly valid \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) must contain \(\mathcal O(N)\) for every \(N\in\mathcal N(H)\) and every compatible \(H\).  The global-atom lemma gives
\[
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)
 =\{\mathcal O(N):N\in\mathcal N(H)\}
\]
at the present \(\alpha\).  Combining the required inclusion \(\mathfrak C_\alpha(H)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_\alpha(H)\) with the just-proved reverse inclusion gives equality at every compatible table.

The theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-weak-order-coverage}\) verifies that the baseline set itself attains the stated uniform coverage.  Since the preceding equality is forced for every \(\alpha\in(0,\delta_\star)\), a family required to be strictly smaller at some compatible table at every nominal level cannot exist.  No step treats \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\), so no conclusion about that regime follows.
body.justification: The theorem gives the faithful negative answer available for consonant closure: low-level strict refinement conflicts with uniform finite-sample coverage even without imposing consonance.
body.gap: The argument is deliberately silent for \(\alpha\ge\delta_\star\), where a strict consonant exact construction may or may not exist.
body.consumer: Software designers can avoid searching for an impossible universal all-level refinement and can confine any closure search to nominal levels not excluded by the atom threshold.
